# GOLEM

> GOLEM is an open-source npm package, `golem-spec`, built for the Kiroween 2026 hackathon (category: Skeleton Crew). It turns the EARS acceptance criteria that Kiro writes in `.kiro/specs/*/requirements.md` into physics property tests that run in MuJoCo (WebAssembly, same engine in Node and the browser). For each requirement it searches for the scenario that breaks it (random Latin-hypercube trials, then cross-entropy search, then shrinking to the mildest failing case), pins the counterexample as a regression seed, and gates Kiro's AI agent with a Stop hook so the agent cannot call a task done while any requirement is false.

## What a visitor can do on this site
- /stagger/ : a live Unitree G1 humanoid (Unitree's published walking policy) in the browser. Drag it to shove it. Click "Summon 64 ghosts" on a requirement to run 64 simulated trials; trials that fall turn red; the verdict shows the smallest push that breaks the requirement and a replay.
- /candy/ : a Franka Panda arm with a suction cup sorting Halloween candy while a child's hand reaches in; safety requirements for speed and separation near the hand.
- /kit/ : the npm package and its CLI (`golem init | check | test | falsify | replay | gate | mcp`), MCP server tools, Kiro hooks, agents, skills, Power and Crew app.
- /evidence/ : measured results with raw data, methods and limits.
- /how-kiro/ : how Kiro built GOLEM (specs, steering, hooks, agents, MCP, audits, what went wrong).

## Key measured facts (all from committed raw data in the repository's evidence/ folder)
- Unitree's published G1 walking policy falls from a 0.2 s pelvis push of 62.5 N from its right side (260°) at 20% of its stride, but holds 240.6 N from behind-left (160°). 36 directions x 5 stride phases x 3 seeds, 4,860 trials.
- The candy arm's first safety controller watched only the suction cup; GOLEM found the wrist flange (link7) ending closer than 0.10 m to a child's hand in 57 of 228 trials.
- Guided search vs random sampling on the G1's requirements: no significant difference at budget 96; at budget 256 on the rarest failure, guided found it in a median 93 trials vs 158.5 (p = 0.26, not significant). On a synthetic 0.11% failure region guided search found it 30/30 vs random 7/30.
- The G1 port matches Unitree's own Python reference run to within 2.5 micrometres after 2 s.

## Install
npm i -D golem-spec
npx golem-spec init
